summary: Inference-time LLM optimization routinely cuts API spend by 50-90% without touching model weights, primarily through caching, compression, and smart model routing. The highest-leverage move is provider prompt caching (zero correctness risk, up to 90% off cached input tokens), layered with exact-match and semantic caching plus model cascading. Teams that instrument hit rate per cache layer and route simple tasks to budget models capture the largest sustained savings.

techniques.name: Provider Prefix / Prompt Caching
techniques.description: Reuses the cached KV state for a repeated prompt prefix (system prompts, few-shot examples, long context) so the provider only charges a fraction for the cached portion. Zero correctness risk since it only reuses identical prefixes. Widely considered the #1 cost-reduction technique.
techniques.example: Put your large static system prompt and few-shot examples at the start of every request; Anthropic caches it (~90% cheaper on hits) while the variable user query stays at the end.

techniques.name: Exact-Match Caching
techniques.description: Caches responses keyed on the exact query string, serving identical repeated queries from a key-value store at sub-millisecond latency and avoiding the LLM inference call entirely.
techniques.example: Hash the full prompt and store the response in Redis with a TTL; on an identical FAQ query, return the cached answer without calling the model.

techniques.name: Semantic Caching
techniques.description: Caches responses for semantically similar prompts rather than exact matches by embedding the query and searching for near-matches above a cosine-similarity threshold (e.g. >0.85). On a hit it bypasses the model entirely, saving both input and output tokens, but requires tuning an acceptable false-positive rate.
techniques.savings: 45% hit rate / up to 50% output-token reduction
techniques.example: Embed 'How do I return a product?' and match it to a cached 'What's your return policy?' at cosine >0.85, returning the stored answer; use vCache-style error-rate guarantees to bound false positives.

techniques.name: Prompt Compression (LLMLingua)
techniques.description: Uses a small model to compress prompts and RAG context by dropping low-information tokens with minimal performance loss, reducing input token count aggressively — especially effective in retrieval-augmented pipelines.
techniques.savings: 20-50% token reduction (reports of up to 20x in RAG)
techniques.example: Run retrieved RAG chunks through LLMLingua before injecting them into the prompt, cutting context tokens ~30% while preserving answer quality.

techniques.name: Smart Model Routing & Cascading
techniques.description: Routes each request to the cheapest model capable of handling it — budget-tier models for simple/classification tasks, flagship models only for complex reasoning — optionally cascading from cheap to expensive on low-confidence outputs.
techniques.example: Send 70% of simple queries to a budget model (e.g. GPT-4o-mini / Haiku / Gemini Flash) and escalate only ambiguous ones to a flagship model.

techniques.name: Batch APIs
techniques.description: Submits non-urgent requests through asynchronous batch endpoints that process within a window (typically 24h) in exchange for a flat discount versus synchronous calls.
techniques.example: Run nightly document summarization jobs through the OpenAI Batch API for an instant 50% discount on both input and output tokens.

techniques.name: Lean Prompt Engineering
techniques.description: Trims verbose instructions, redundant examples, and bloated context files to shrink per-call token counts across every request.
techniques.example: Cap your CLAUDE.md / rules file under 5,000 tokens and use /compact at natural phase boundaries to compress agent context.

techniques.name: Structured Outputs & JSON Schemas
techniques.description: Constrains the model to emit only structured data via JSON schema / structured output modes, eliminating verbose prose and reducing output tokens while improving parse reliability.
techniques.example: Request a JSON schema with only the three fields you need instead of a free-form explanation, cutting output length and downstream parsing errors.

techniques.name: Session Context Management
techniques.description: Maintains conversation state efficiently — summarizing or pruning older turns instead of resending the full history — to avoid quadratic token growth in long chats.
techniques.example: After N turns, replace the raw history with a running summary so each new request carries a compact context rather than the entire transcript.

techniques.name: KV Cache Management (Infrastructure)
techniques.description: Server-side techniques for self-hosted inference, organized by a March 2026 Dell survey into cache eviction (dropping low-importance tokens), cache compression (quantization/pooling), hybrid memory (offloading to CPU/NVMe), and novel attention mechanisms (linear/log-linear attention).
techniques.savings: Varies; higher throughput & lower memory per request
techniques.example: Enable KV-cache quantization and CPU offloading in vLLM to serve longer contexts on the same GPU, raising throughput and lowering per-token infra cost.

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic caching library for LLM apps; stores embeddings and returns cached responses for similar queries across many providers.
tools.pricing_paid: Free (open source; self-hosted infra costs only)

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Unified proxy/SDK for 100+ LLM providers with built-in caching, model routing/fallbacks, cost tracking, and rate limiting via an OpenAI-compatible API.
tools.pricing_paid: Free open source; Enterprise tier with SSO/support (custom pricing)

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: LLM observability and cost-monitoring proxy with caching, request logging, prompt management, and per-model spend analytics.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier (10k req/mo); Pro from ~$20/mo, Enterprise custom

tools.name: Redis (LLM / Semantic Cache)
tools.description: In-memory data store powering exact-match, semantic, and session caching with sub-millisecond latency and vector similarity search for multi-tier LLM caching.
tools.pricing_paid: Free OSS; Redis Cloud free tier then usage-based (from ~$5/mo), Enterprise custom

tools.name: LangChain
tools.description: LLM application framework with built-in caching integrations (in-memory, Redis, SQLite, semantic), prompt templating, and model routing abstractions.
tools.pricing_paid: Free open source; LangSmith observability from ~$39/user/mo

tools.name: LLMLingua
tools.description: Microsoft open-source prompt-compression toolkit that reduces prompt/RAG context tokens with minimal quality loss using a small compression model.

tools.name: vCache
tools.description: Semantic cache that returns cached responses for similar prompts under user-defined error-rate guarantees, bounding false-positive risk.

tools.name: OpenRouter
tools.description: Unified API gateway across many model providers enabling smart routing, fallbacks, and price-based model selection from a single endpoint.
tools.pricing_paid: Pay-as-you-go passthrough pricing plus small routing fee

tools.name: vLLM
tools.description: High-throughput open-source inference server with PagedAttention and KV-cache optimizations (quantization, prefix caching) for self-hosted open-weight models.
tools.pricing_paid: Free (open source; your own GPU/infra costs)

quick_wins: Turn on provider prompt/prefix caching and place all static content (system prompt, few-shot examples, long context) at the front of every request for up to 90% off cached input tokens.
Add an exact-match cache (Redis) in front of your API to serve repeated/FAQ queries at zero model cost.
Route simple and classification tasks to a budget-tier model (GPT-4o-mini / Claude Haiku / Gemini Flash) and reserve flagship models for complex reasoning.
Move all non-urgent/offline workloads (summaries, enrichment, evals) to a provider Batch API for an instant ~50% discount.
Trim prompts and context aggressively — cap rules/system files, request JSON-only structured outputs, and summarize old conversation turns to cut tokens on every call.
